summary: Model family choice meaningfully affects predictive performance on the Adult Income dataset. The best model (Gradient Boosting) achieves ROC-AUC of 0.9210, while the worst (Decision Tree) achieves 0.7489, a difference of 0.1721 (23.0%). This effect is stable across repeated cross-validation.
direction: Gradient Boosting > Decision Tree (model family choice matters)
methodological_choices: Preprocessing: Label-encoded categorical features, StandardScaler for SVM/KNN/LogReg. Models: LogisticRegression, DecisionTree, RandomForest, GradientBoosting, SVM, KNN, GaussianNB. Validation: 5-fold stratified CV on original features; repeated 10-fold CV (5 seeds) for stability. Metric: ROC-AUC (handles class imbalance well). Random state fixed at 42 for reproducibility.
verification_method: Repeated 10-fold stratified cross-validation with 5 different random seeds (50 total folds per model)
verification_result: Finding held up: performance differences remained consistent. Best model Gradient Boosting (μ=0.9210, 95% CI=[0.9132, 0.9279]) vs worst model Decision Tree (μ=0.7489, 95% CI=[0.7335, 0.7636]). No CI overlap between models, indicating statistically significant differences.
